title: YNX DEX — Non-custodial Pools and Verifiable Execution
metaDescription: Inspect consensus-committed YNX DEX assets, pools, swaps and liquidity state. Public execution remains gated until the v13 chain migration and Wallet registry entry are approved.
h1: Consensus-native liquidity, bounded by Wallet approval
summary: YNX DEX v13 stores Testnet assets, balances, constant-product pools, LP shares, swaps and audit events in deterministic consensus state. The Web/PWA reads only AppHash-bound gateway envelopes and never handles private keys.
features: Consensus-native Testnet assets, balances, CPMM pools, LP shares, swaps and audit events
AppHash-bound v13 gateway reads with strict source and version verification
Deterministic integer exact-input quotes matching direct consensus pool math
Non-custodial constant-product and two-asset StableSwap pool candidates
User-owned Strategy Vault with bounded engine mandates
Direct StableSwap swap and liquidity actions without standing pool approvals
FairFlow intent and solver competition candidate
Dynamic LP protection and depeg circuit-breaker candidate
Source-labelled Indexer API and JavaScript SDK
Authenticated immutable point-in-time Indexer recovery bundle and isolated restore drill
riskDisclosures: The consensus DEX is pending protected-branch review, node migration and public cutover; the current public chain must not be represented as v13 until those gates complete.
Wallet transaction handoff remains fail-closed until the canonical registry entry and callback verification are approved.
Unaudited software; no independent smart-contract audit is complete.
No verified YNX Testnet deployment, reviewed liquidity or public transaction proof exists.
No public runtime, hosted download or production-signed artifact exists.
The local point-in-time recovery drill does not establish operational RPO for a provisioned Testnet indexer.
StableSwap requires reviewed assets and Oracle/depeg policy before deployment.
FairFlow and LP protection remain local candidates with additional public-network and adversarial requirements.
Cryptographic approvals and transaction submission remain unavailable until canonical Wallet and Gateway integration is accepted.
No yield, APY, price, profit, volume, liquidity or revenue guarantee is made.

faq.question: Does YNX DEX hold user funds?
faq.answer: No. The design is non-custodial. Assets remain in the user wallet, an explicitly approved protocol pool, or the user-owned Strategy Vault. The DEX front end and execution adapter do not receive private keys or unrestricted withdrawal authority.

faq.question: Is YNX DEX live on Mainnet?
faq.answer: No. This package is an unaudited local Testnet preview candidate. Mainnet, public deployment, verified liquidity and public transaction evidence are all false.

faq.question: What is a Strategy Vault?
faq.answer: A user-owned vault that permits only reviewed tokens, pools, methods and limits for a limited engine session. The owner can pause, revoke, kill, withdraw or use emergency exit.

faq.question: Can the Quant Engine move funds anywhere?
faq.answer: No. The adapter creates typed requests only. Vault contracts reject arbitrary transfers, owner changes, unlimited approvals and actions outside the mandate.

faq.question: Does YNX DEX promise APY or best price?
faq.answer: No. Quotes and execution proofs must be source-labelled and time-bounded. The product does not publish fake APY, guarantee profit or hide spread.
